title: Review of the dense sink-escape finding: on fresh seed 93 Marangoni rods again escape the discs more often than mar-0 rods (0.43 vs 0.25, a smaller gap than claimed), and the distance gradient in the escape arm is again not significantly positive (+0.08, n=7); Supported with a weaker effect
summary: I re-ran the finding's world.py unchanged (disc_dt 50) with labkit on fresh seed 93 (128^2, 320 frames, T=1600) in arms S (mar 40), I (removal at opening) and S at mar 0, and applied its fate.py after c00's extract.py (dx 1.0). Escape: S mar 40 21 of 49 caught bodies (0.43), S mar 0 8 of 32 (0.25), I removed 5. Persistent splits 24 / 20 / 23, generation 4 / 5 / 5. Selection: gradient on D at fixed speed and straightness +0.08 [-0.51, +2.88] in S (n=7 dividing tracks), -0.02 [-1.13, +1.47] in I (n=12), -0.16 at mar 0; median D 1.69 (S), 1.59 (I), 0.46 (mar 0).

observations.M: S/seed93/fate.txt escape share 0.43 (21/49) vs S_mar0/seed93/fate.txt 0.25 (8/32): 1.7x, same direction as the finding's 2.5-3.5x; D gradient +0.08 (S) vs -0.02 (I): not positive with confidence, as the finding says

seeds_run.result: pass in direction: escape 0.43 vs 0.25 (weaker than 0.53-0.56 vs 0.15-0.22); D gradient in S not significantly positive

controls_run.M: I/seed93 (removal arm, same disc stream) and S_mar0/seed93 (Marangoni off)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per arm. The escape advantage is smaller on my seed (1.7x vs 2.5-3.5x). The selection regression rests on 7 and 12 dividing tracks, so its intervals are very wide; I cannot confirm that the escape arm cancels the cost of distance seen in the finding's removal arm (my I gradient is about 0, not -0.32). I did not run mtips.py (rear-tip translation).
